review.notes: No code fences in the OCR, so no fence-swallowing; all seven physical PDF pages were compared line-by-line (normalized) against the OCR Markdown, and page 1, page 5 (benchmark table) and page 7 (contact email) were additionally rendered for visual verification. The benchmark table values 0.314 / 0.553 / 0.33 / 0.651 (POV=1200) and the ExploitGym row match the print. The OCR string 'MAI-Cyber-Flash-1' on physical p.5 reproduces a transposition printed in the source PDF itself, so it is an author typo, not an OCR defect. The printed cover title 'MAI-Cyber-1-Flash' is not repeated in the OCR body; the reader page already carries the metadata title 'MAI-Cyber-1-Flash Model Card', so no patch was made. List bullets are recorded as escaped hyphens (\-) where the print uses bullets; visible text is unaffected.

patches.evidence: Rendered physical p.7 (300 dpi crop) prints the contact address as MSFTAIActRequest@microsoft.com; OCR dropped the t of 'Act' and reads MSFTAIAcRequest@microsoft.com.

Rendered physical p.5 'External Cyber Benchmark Results' table shows the CyberSecEval4 cell as two separate lines ('Threat Intel: 0.553' and 'Malware Analysis: 0.33'); OCR concatenated them into one run-on string '0.553Malware'. The patch inserts the printed line break inside the raw HTML table cell and changes no characters.
